items.statement: Final conclusion: formation competition and stability jointly favor the major isomer
items.expected: The final answer integrates actual formation-channel comparisons and neutral-product stability to establish that major forms more readily and is more stable in the model studied, using both lines of evidence to explain the supplied regioselectivity. Distinguish unfavorable comparator formation/stability from a strictly zero yield. Hydrogen-bonding/steric causation that has not been independently decomposed is not a mandatory answer, and a pathway must not be inferred solely from a low product energy.

items.statement: Final conclusion: redistribution from minor to major is thermodynamically driven
items.expected: Use actual neutral-product G comparisons to determine that the thermodynamic redistribution direction from P3 toward P2 is favorable, and distinguish this from competition in initial formation. Reproducing undisclosed experimental endpoints is not required. Product G alone must not be used to claim that complete exchange kinetics, full equilibrium or rates have been calculated.
